answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks through speed-of-light distance bounding. Nodes must answer cryptographic challenges within nanosecond windows to prove unique physical locations relative to network beacons. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of deploying discrete transceivers, unable to forge multiple coordinates from one ferrous enclosure. However, signal blockages from a rocky knoll or a dense grove cause latency delays that can exclude legitimate agents.
